params.prompt: The product is a measurement, not a mood — this switch set was tested, not just marketed as quiet. A mechanical keyboard switch set and its matched desk mat laid out on a measurement rig on a matte-black surface, shot top-down or at a low instrument angle under hard directional light. A visible metal ruler or scale bar runs along one edge of the frame as a measurement reference. A small dB-meter or waveform readout graphic sits near the switches, its digits picked out in calibration yellow — the only color accent in the frame. Composition is wide/landscape with the subject occupying the lower-center to center of the frame and generous clear matte-black space across the upper third, left open for a headline to be placed later; nothing in that upper zone competes with where text would sit. Reads like a photo pulled off a calibration bench, not a mood board — precise, plain, instrument-grade. Matte black and instrument grey dominate; calibration yellow (#FFC800) appears exactly once, on the dB figure or a tick mark, never as a fill or gradient. Hard, clinical lighting like a lab or test-bench photo, not warm ambient window light. No soft shadows, no bokeh, no styled props.
